source: Stated by the author on 2026-11-26 from the current version of the companion volume. Theorem and page numbers refer to that version.

companion_volume.title: Rigorous Construction of 4D Yang-Mills QFT and the Mass Gap (GZYM)
companion_volume.note: The cited version is not in the repository or the project. The project copy GZYM_proof_2_section2closed_v4.tex (dated March 2026) lacks the cited sections, so the references are recorded as stated and have not been checked against the text.

os_axioms.statement: Osterwalder-Schrader axioms OS0-OS4 for the continuum Schwinger functions on R^4
os_axioms.assumed_or_open: Theorem 2.1 is stated for a compact simple Lie group and assumes a proved weak-to-physical RG trajectory on the physical quotient, including horizon matching; continuum estimates and identification of the gauge-invariant Schwinger functions with ordinary Yang-Mills; and, on the finite SU(3) route, completion of its six-channel crossing, external-norm and Feshbach gates. The notice above Theorem 37.10 leaves continuum regularity and full Euclidean covariance open, and Theorem A.34.11 does not close those prerequisites.

reflection_positivity.statement: Reflection positivity of the continuum theory on the gauge-invariant sector
reflection_positivity.proved: Theorem A.67.1: for fixed finite beta >= 0 and subsequences of even periodic four-dimensional SU(3) Wilson boxes, positivity on the gauge-invariant continuous local algebra, tested on the reflected half-lattice.
reflection_positivity.assumed_or_open: The continuum gate is open. Theorem 40.20 assumes joint positivity for the localized Gribov-Zwanziger measure and that reflection preserves the Gribov region; p. 269 and Lemma A.67.3 withdraw the generic reweighting argument. This is not positivity of the gauge-fixed gluon propagator, which lattice data show to be violated (Cucchieri, Mendes, Taurines, arXiv:hep-lat/0406020, Landau gauge, 3d SU(2)).

rg_convergence.statement: Limit of zero lattice spacing and infinite volume
rg_convergence.proved: Theorem A.67.1 takes the volume to infinity at fixed cutoff only, along subsequences and without uniqueness.
rg_convergence.assumed_or_open: Theorem 40.10 is conditional. Lemmas 40.12-40.13 and Theorem 40.14 require matched relevant and marginal couplings, control of generated differences along the actual RG flow, and a scale-dependent continuity error that tends to zero; Remarks A.67.5-A.67.6 explain why the printed bounds do not establish those steps.

spectral_gap.statement: Physical mass gap Delta > 0, uniform in the volume
spectral_gap.proved: A decay bound at fixed volume, whose infimum over volumes is zero (Remark A.67.6).
spectral_gap.assumed_or_open: Theorem 25.2 and Proposition A.66.7 require a common positive time-decay rate on a dense centered physical core, not decay of one observable. Theorem A.67.7 also requires convergence to an OS-reconstructible theory and a rate bounded away from zero in physical units, uniformly in the spatial volume. The Faddeev-Popov bound of Theorem 8.12 is not the physical Hamiltonian gap.
